title: WWII PUBLICATIONS ETC
reason: Under-described 'etc': a Don McLean concert poster with an apparent hand signature (unverified, no COA) plus five WWII Australian service publications in original postal boxes.
findings: Title is only 'WWII PUBLICATIONS ETC'. Photo 1 shows six wartime Australian Army-looking items: four cardboard postal boxes printed 'KHAKI and GREEN..', 'STAND EASY', 'ACTIVE SERVICE' and 'JUNGLE WARFARE' (each has a printed box panel at top right that looks like a postage-paid stamp box and a stuck-on typed or handwritten dispatch label, text not legible at this resolution); a red cloth hardback 'SOLDIERING ON' with a crest and small print at the lower right that I could not read; and a torn paper-covered booklet titled 'VICTORY' (script above it appears to read 'New Guinea') with an orange sunburst badge (looks like the Army Rising Sun) at the lower edge. No publisher, date or edition is legible, so WWII dating is plausible from style and badge but not confirmed. Photos 2 and 3 are close-ups of a glossy concert poster that the title does not mention at all: 'Live in Concert - DON McLEAN - America's Music Legend - featuring American Pie, Vincent, Crying and much more... - A John L Hansen - Event Entertainment Presentation', with a black pen signature reading 'Don McLean' on the white strip at the foot. The signature looks like a continuous ink line with varied pressure rather than a printed dot pattern, but this is a low-resolution photo and there is no certificate, dedication, date or witness, so it is unverified. I could not research the boxed series or signed-poster values (web search budget was used up), so the strength rests on the photos only.
condition: Poster is glossy with visible fold lines and ripples, no tears seen. Boxes are worn, stained and creased, with a torn corner on ACTIVE SERVICE and a chipped corner on JUNGLE WARFARE; contents of the boxes are not shown. VICTORY booklet is torn, stained and missing a piece at the lower edge. SOLDIERING ON cover looks sound with some rubbing.
rescore_note: Six worn WWII-era Australian Army items (postal boxes 'Khaki and Green', 'Stand Easy', 'Active Service', 'Jungle Warfare', a red 'Soldiering On' hardback, a torn 'New Guinea Victory' booklet, box contents unknown) plus a creased Don McLean tour poster with a plausible but uncertified pen signature, heavily discounted because there is no COA; my estimate about $80 to $150, no comps found (web search budget was used up).
